newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: LONRHO SELLS ZAMBIA BREWERIES STAKE.
newsitem.headline: LONRHO SELLS ZAMBIA BREWERIES STAKE.

text.p: Lonrho Plc has sold its 70 percent stake in Northern Breweries to Central African Holdings seven months after buying it from the Zambian government, the Zambia Privatisation Agency (ZPA) said on Wednesday.

"On February 12, 1997, Lonrho sold off their interest in Northern Breweries to Central African Holdings, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Madvhani Group of Uganda, who are also owners and operators of Nile Breweries," ZPA said in a statement.
It said the sale had been necessitated by the acquisition of a "small but significant stake" by Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd -- which own Zambia Breweries -- in Lonrho.

"ZPA was duly concerned about having both Zambian Breweries and Northern Breweries controlled by Anglo American, which would not meet the cabinet's directive that the two breweries should not be owned by the same organisation in order to ensure competition," the spokesman said.
Lonrho had earlier indicated that Anglo was only interested in Lonrho's mining assets.

It said Lonrho would be split into two companies - one containing the mining interests in which Anglo would have a substantial interest, and another containing the non-mining interests in which Anglo would have no interest.
"As a protective measure, the sale agreement with Lonrho had a clause indicating that Lonrho planned to accomplish the demerger," ZPA said.
"As of December 1996, it became clear that the demerger would not take place, due to changes in the ownership and strategic management of Lonrho," it added.
ZPA said Lonrho had to sell its stake in the breweries without a profit since the breweries financial condition had deteriorated under Lonrho due to lack of investment.
Lonrho acquired Northern Breweries for $9 million with a forward investment package of $17.8 million last year.
Madhvani Group had committed itself to spend at least $8 million to upgrade Northern Breweries to international standards, ZPA said.
"This investment has already begun. Further investment above the $8 million already committed to, will be provided as market forces so require," ZPA said.
